visual_features.color: dark grey to blackish body, silvery-grey shimmer, pale grey underparts
visual_features.body_shape: slender primate with long tail, prominent pointed crest on crown
visual_features.distinctive_marks: tall pointed crest on crown (spiky hairdo), long tail exceeding body length, pale eyebrow stripe

description: The silvery lutung, also known as the silvered leaf monkey or silvery langur, is an Old World monkey (family Cercopithecidae). It is arboreal, living in coastal, mangrove, and riverine forests across Sumatra, Borneo, Java, the southwestern Malay Peninsula, Natuna Islands, and other nearby islands. It is a specialist folivore with 91% of its diet consisting of leaves. It has a large three-chambered stomach for digesting cellulose, similar to ruminants. Diurnal and social, it lives in harem groups of 9-40 individuals with one adult male and multiple females. The social structure is matrilineal. It is listed as Vulnerable on the IUCN Red List due to extensive habitat loss from deforestation, oil palm plantations, and forest fires.
population_estimate: The population is decreasing due to extensive habitat loss from deforestation, oil palm plantations, and forest fires across its range in Sumatra, Borneo, Java, and the Malay Peninsula. Listed as Vulnerable (VU) on the IUCN Red List.
habitat: Arboreal, inhabiting coastal, mangrove, and riverine forests. Found across Sumatra, Borneo, Java, the southwestern Malay Peninsula, the Natuna Islands, and nearby islands. It prefers mangrove swamps and nearby forest regions and generally avoids travelling far from coasts or rivers.
ecosystem_role: As a specialist folivore, it helps shape forest vegetation dynamics through selective feeding. It disperses seeds of fruit consumed in their diet. Their presence indicates healthy mangrove and riverine forest ecosystems. Mixed-species groups with proboscis monkeys have been observed in Borneo.
human_connection: These monkeys are indicators of healthy coastal and mangrove ecosystems, which protect shorelines and support fisheries. Deforestation for oil palm plantations across Southeast Asia is their greatest threat. There are known hybrids between silvery lutungs and proboscis monkeys in Borneo due to habitat fragmentation from oil palm cultivation.
what_students_can_do: Learn about the importance of mangrove and coastal forest conservation
Support sustainable palm oil practices by choosing certified products
Share information about this species to raise awareness
fun_fact: The fur appears silvery due to grey-tipped dark hairs, giving it a unique shimmering coat that inspired its name.
It has a specialized three-chambered stomach to digest tough leaves, similar to the digestive system of cows.
Infants are born with bright orange fur and pale pink skin, which gradually transforms to a silver coat over several months.
It has been observed forming mixed-species groups and even hybridizing with proboscis monkeys in Borneo's fragmented forests.
